title: Miguel Fernández Durán to the marqués de San Felipe, El Pardo 30 Nov 1718 (ACA Diversos, Legación en Génova y Turín, Cajón 1 leg. 22 doc. 67; DECODE R10181)

documents.shelfmark: Archivo de la Corona de Aragón, Diversos, Legación en Génova y Turín, Cajón 1, leg. 22, doc. 67; DECODE R10181

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the four DECODE images; the only clear text is the cover, the closing formula and the signature.

transcription.source: NoAutopilot's two-pass reconciled transcription (309 groups), checked here on the DECODE images; the missing last line of f2v (8 groups) added here.
transcription.notes: 7 written as ')', 9 as a tailed 'ɔ', 4 as a triangle, 5 as 'S'; 2/9/7 confusions graded R or M.

system.summary: A numerical code, values 2-768 (one 877), dot-separated, no marks; the range fits a code of about 770-880 entries. Whether it is one-part (alphabetical) is open: the legation's 1715 Acquaviva key R10193 is one-part, and Brice Dudout suggested de 163, del 164, que 652, but no passage reads under that.

prior_solution.where: Cryptoole XX1718-2 open; DECODE Non-decrypted, no document attached; NoAutopilot cipher-lab 'blocked'

conditions.human_role: Selected the target (catalogue 355 solve brief); the DECODE session cookie was supplied earlier.
tools: one-part code annealer (mono.py) with a Spanish word-bigram model

solution.what: Downloaded the DECODE pages R10181-R10197 and the images of R10181 and the nine keys R10189-R10197 with the saved cookie.
Took NoAutopilot's 309-group transcription, checked the digit shapes on f2r ll. 2-4 and f2v, and added the last line of f2v that it lacked (8 groups): 317 groups, 149 distinct.
Cryptoole snapshot (XX1718-2 open), DECODE record (no document), NoAutopilot's search log, web search: no decipherment or edition.

Tested the nine legation keys R10189-R10197 (1711-1718) by range (27-65% of the groups in range) and applied R10194, the Monteleón-Villamayor key that names the war secretariat, to the in-range groups: nonsense (32 = G eleven times).

Enciphered a 317-word Vasto-memoirs passage in a one-part code of the 700 commonest corpus words (2-770) and ran the order-constrained annealer: 49% and 60% of tokens right on two seeds, mostly function words.

Ran the one-part annealer on the letter, ascending, descending, and ascending with Brice Dudout's anchors de 163, del 164, que 652 fixed: word salad every time (best -1497.5 anchored, -1499.5 ascending, -1557.9 descending).

outcome.method_basis: A numerical code of about 770-880 entries, 317 groups; none of the nine legation keys on DECODE fits, nothing is in print, and the one-part ciphertext-only annealer reads only 49-60% of a function-word control and gives word salad on the letter.
outcome.notes: Blocked on the key: needs the 1718 war-office code (ACA Cajón 19 leg. 30 docs not on DECODE, AGS Guerra/Estado) or San Felipe's deciphered register.

credits.note: two-pass transcription of R10181 and value ranges of the nine keys
the nine keys are for other correspondents; suggested an alphabetical word code of about 880 entries
